column4: Shows that a valid Rule 56 pass closes the party's window and removes the opportunity from later availability.
Shows that fixed payload defaults are inserted before execution at the public decision boundary.
Shows the public pass path updates state only through pass bookkeeping.
Shows that the filed-phase generator includes Rule 12 after a complaint and before an answer or Rule 12 motion.
Shows that `applyDecision` returns `NO_CURRENT_OPPORTUNITY` for a closed case.
Shows that the accepted dismissal action closes the case and stops the engine on the next query.
Confines the returned action to the selected opportunity's role, tool, and payload.
Shows that an accepted tool decision yields exactly the executable action selected by the current opportunity.
Shows that every later decision returns `NO_CURRENT_OPPORTUNITY` after an authorized execution closes the case.
Shows that case initialization records the complaint, docket entry, and initial trace in one state.
Shows that case initialization records the complaint attachments.
Shows that a jurisdiction dismissal leaves no next opportunity.
Shows that a jurisdiction dismissal closes the case and records a docket entry.
Shows that the public decision boundary emits the judge's jurisdiction-dismissal action in the defective filed case.
Identifies the judge's jurisdiction-dismissal opportunity as current in a defective filed case.
Shows that jurisdiction dismissal outranks Rule 12, rejects an out-of-order party decision, and closes the case.
Shows that later merits attempts fail once jurisdiction dismissal closes the case.
Shows that jurisdiction dismissal closes a filed case and terminates opportunity generation.
Shows that the selector prioritizes the judge's jurisdiction duty in a defective filed case.
Shows that Rule 12 remains available even while the selector chooses jurisdiction dismissal first.
Shows that an enabled jurisdiction screen emits exactly one deterministic dismissal candidate.
Shows that the same defective diversity allegations produce no dismissal candidate in International Claw District.
Shows that the International Claw profile disables the federal jurisdiction screen in the defect detector.
Combines priority selection, role partition, and case closure at the public boundary.
Shows that once selection fixes the current opportunity, every other role is rejected.
Shows that closure removes every available opportunity.
Shows that closure eliminates the selector result used by the decision boundary.
Connects the public next-opportunity API to the selector.
Characterizes termination in terms of the open-opportunity selector.
Shows that `nextOpportunity` is terminal for a closed case.
Shows that the International Claw profile selects the defendant's Rule 12 opportunity and omits jurisdiction dismissal.
Shows that defective diversity pleading under the federal profile selects the judge's dismissal opportunity before defendant pleading.
Shows that the International Claw open opportunity set contains no jurisdiction-dismissal tool.
Shows that the federal profile treats residence-only diversity pleading and a $108 amount as facially defective.
Shows that the International Claw profile removes the federal subject-matter Rule 12 ground.
Shows that judgment entry copies the jury verdict amount and sets the case status to `judgment_entered`.
Shows that a granted for-cause ruling removes one candidate and records that juror as excused for cause.
Shows that empanelment preserves each juror's id, name, note, model, and persona file.
Shows that once questionnaires and oral questioning are complete for every remaining candidate, the judge can empanel the jury.
Shows that a peremptory strike removes exactly one candidate from the panel and records the targeted juror as struck.
Shows that a defense verdict carries zero damages even if some jurors proposed plaintiff-side amounts.
Shows that verdict derivation cannot run until every sworn juror has cast a ballot in the current round.
Shows that a changed split advances to another ballot round when neither side reaches the threshold.
Checks that vote storage order does not affect the representative plaintiff-majority verdict.
Defines the plaintiff-side damages aggregation rule: the verdict amount is the mean of plaintiff-vote damages.
Shows that an unchanged split in consecutive rounds produces a hung jury.
Shows that reopening the Rule 56 window restores eligibility when the ordinary prerequisites still hold.
Captures the exact objective prerequisites for Rule 56 eligibility.
Shows that Rule 56 window closure persists across unrelated pretrial activity and reopens only on amendment.
Shows that judgment entry on a jury case requires the `verdict` disposition.
